systems.name: Boot & orchestration
systems.responsibility: The wiring spine: main.js boots the game, builds the callbacks/deps bundles that connect every other system, and owns the render loop entry. gameSession authors the netcode bridge.

edges.detail: main.js:314 Netcode.registerGameCallbacks(buildNetcodeGameBridge(…)) merges ~40 real impls over netcode.js's default stub `callbacks` object.
main.js:4748 runGameLoop(loopState, callbacks) — every frame decision inside is deps.isHost()/deps.getRoundState()/deps.runFixedPhysicsStep().
main.js:2149 initLevelManager(dependencies) — the ~20-property LevelManagerDeps typedef is the contract.

notes: src/main.js is a ~5.6k-line root; `async function main()` is one closure (~lines 714–5219) holding ~84 unexported inner functions that escape ONLY via the callbacks/deps bundles.
buildNetcodeGameBridge (gameSession.js) is the authoring site for the netcode callbacks seam — the real place to learn which main.js impl backs a callbacks.* name.
config.js owns CART_COLORS + the CONFIG knob table (an invariant surface — do not modify CART_COLORS or the material traverse logic).

systems.name: Game loop & flow
systems.responsibility: The fixed-step frame loop, round phase machine, and per-round clock. Runs physics/present decisions through injected deps and schedules Living Store directives.

edges.detail: deps.runFixedPhysicsStep({…}) / deps.getSimulationCallbacks(true) drive the host sim each fixed step.
directives/directiveEngine.js:88 subscribes to gameStore for mid-round directive scheduling.

notes: runGameLoop receives a deps bundle (GameLoopState / PhysicsStepDeps typedefs) rather than importing main.js — the call graph is main.js → runGameLoop → deps.* → back into main.js.
directiveEngine subscribes to gameStore; a gameStore shape change silently changes directive scheduling.

systems.name: Physics simulation
systems.responsibility: Host-authoritative Rapier3D world: cart bodies, colliders, the fixed-step integrate, and the single Rapier collision callback that seeds KO/fall events.

edges.detail: collision/fall detection raises KO events consumed by src/scoring/ reactors (koEvent/koReactors).
host sim results flow out through the netcode callbacks bundle (kill confirm, teleport-to-spawn, material updates).

notes: Rapier is host-AUTHORITATIVE, not host-exclusive: the host is sole authority for NPCs and remote inputs, but every predicting client steps the same world locally (gameLoop.js client-prediction branch). The server never simulates — zero Rapier in party/.
Bot AI lives INSIDE simulation.js and gameFlow.js — there is no separate bots module.

One Rapier collision callback: eventQueue.drainCollisionEvents((h1,h2,started)=>…) in simulation.js (~line 2717). world.castRay reads .handle off exclude args — pass Collider/RigidBody objects, never raw handles.

systems.name: AI bots (virtual)
systems.responsibility: Solo NPC support. Only the rubberband assist has its own module; the actual bot decision logic is embedded in simulation.js and gameFlow.js, not extracted.

edges.detail: soloRubberband is applied inside the host sim step (solo rooms only).

notes: bot logic lives inside simulation.js and gameFlow.js — there is no bots module
soloRubberband is solo-gated; it must not leak into multiplayer (verified-healthy item in project-state §5).

systems.name: Networking (client)
systems.responsibility: Client netcode: partysocket control-plane, WebRTC P2P gameplay plane, host-transform interpolation, client prediction rewind-and-replay, and host-migration handoff.

edges.detail: MSG.* control-plane dispatch over the partysocket WebSocket (join/colorPick/readyToggle/hostRound/SDP/ICE).
P2P.sendToAll (host) / P2P.sendToPeer(hostId,…) (client) carry hostTransform, clientInput, spill; kill-feed rides the snapshot JSON tail.
internal netcode game hooks are backed by main.js impls merged in via buildNetcodeGameBridge.

notes: netcode.js declares a module-scope `let callbacks = {…}` (~line 230) of ~40 no-op stubs, replaced once at startup via registerGameCallbacks. Every game hook is invisible to grep.
The client MSG.* dispatch mirror chain lives in netcode.js (~lines 2070–2434); pair each branch with its party/index.ts twin.
Real-time telemetry (hostTransform 40Hz, clientInput, spill) is P2P (netcode/p2p.js) — never route it back through the WebSocket.

systems.name: Networking (server)
systems.responsibility: The partyserver Durable Object: room + WebSocket lifecycle, slot management, ready-up/round lifecycle, WebRTC signaling + TURN minting, host selection, round validation, connection reaping.

edges.detail: server broadcasts MSG.gameStart / hostSpawn / lobby + relays SDP/ICE back to clients over the WebSocket.
message keys + round constants are single-sourced from shared/ (protocol.js, roundConstants.js, readiness.js).

notes: The server NEVER simulates physics (invariant). CartRaveServer.onMessage (index.ts ~line 801, ~450 lines) is a flat if(type===MSG.x) chain with bodies inlined.
room.getConnections() returns an iterator — spread or for…of, never .map().join().

Pure helpers (hostSelection, roundValidation, rateLimit, connectionReaper, hostRearm, slotReconcile) + party/constants.ts thresholds are unit-tested; A5b DO harness lives in tests/party-do/ (Workers Vitest pool).

systems.name: Rendering & post-FX
systems.responsibility: Three.js scene assembly, the EffectComposer post chain (RenderPass → OutputPass → Bloom → Arcade/VHS → FXAA on the default display pipe), contact shadows, the shared Draco loader, and the quality/LOD tier machinery.

edges.detail: scene/frameVisuals consume arena meshes + reactive lights built by levelManager and the level modules.
postFxDebug / gameplayTunePane read + tweak the composer uniforms and quality tiers live.

notes: Composer path, DEFAULT (?bloompipe=display): RenderPass → OutputPass → Bloom → Arcade(VHS) → FXAA. ?bloompipe=hdr swaps to Bloom → OutputPass; OutputPass is never last in either path. toneMapping is a no-op into composer RTs without OutputPass — except on the lowest tier, which bypasses the composer entirely (composerBypass) and tone-maps natively.
Half-res bloom RTs; strength compensated via bloomHalfResStrengthMul. VFX-1 closed: display-referred byte mips.
material.envMapIntensity is a no-op against scene.environment — use scene.environmentIntensity.
frameVisuals.js is cross-cutting (secondary owner: vfx); it lives here as the per-frame present owner.

edges.detail: levelManager is driven entirely through the LevelManagerDeps bundle passed from main.js (performLevelLoad, finalizeArenaForPlay, warmupAfterLevelSwap, …).
level modules + arenaCatalog select per-arena music/ambience beds.

notes: Levels load through LEVEL_IMPORTERS in src/levels/index.js (~line 16) — a dynamic id→import() table, NOT a barrel. The four level modules are reachable only through it.
initLevelManager consumes the ~20-property LevelManagerDeps typedef — read it before touching level swaps.
arenaCatalog.js is the pure-data authoring source for labels/themes/music/ambience/unlocks (D-CONTENT-1).

edges.detail: audioManager.js:20 subscribes to audioStore; announcerDirector.js:341 subscribes to gameStore.

edges.detail: cartrave:menu / cartrave:round-started custom events cross between the menu DOM and main.js (~13 sites).

edges.detail: sampled input axes are read by the host sim; client input is sent P2P per 60Hz fixed-step sample.
touchControls (nipplejs) + haptics feed the same input axes on mobile.

notes: No camera lerp/slerp smoothing — intentionally removed, do not reintroduce (invariant).
simulation.js reads axis.turn/axis.forward as an analog deflection; keyboard eases -1/0/1 to match the stick (INPUT-KB-1, 0.07s attack / 0.05s release).

edges.detail: gameplayAnalytics + gameplayDiagnostics subscribe to gameStore/challengeStore/unlockStore to observe play.

notes: Diagnostics globals namespace is __cc* (__ccTest / __ccDiag / __ccLoopDbg). F8 (or auto on error+assert) captures a bug bundle.

systems.boot-and-orchestration: Adding a hook that main() should provide means adding it to the callbacks/deps bundle too, or it never escapes the closure. Do not carve main.js ad-hoc — that's MAIN-1.
systems.networking-client: Add a netcode hook in THREE places (netcode.js callbacks literal → registerGameCallbacks adapter → buildNetcodeGameBridge); the adapter renames, so literal and bridge keys differ. MSG.* lives once in shared/protocol.js — never duplicate it. Never route hostTransform/clientInput/spill through the WebSocket.
systems.networking-server: Relay + validation + lifecycle only — never simulate physics. Iterate getConnections() with for…of. No migration-model rewrite pre-ship.
systems.physics-simulation: Host-authoritative — clients predict with the same world; the host owns NPCs + remote inputs. castRay exclude takes the object not .handle. Do not move collision logic server-side. Bot logic edits live here (no bots module).
systems.arenas-levels: Change level swaps only through the LevelManagerDeps contract; add levels to LEVEL_IMPORTERS (not a barrel import). Arena content is data in arenaCatalog.js.
systems.rendering-and-postfx: Preserve composer pass order (OutputPass before Arcade; toneMapping depends on it). Bloom's position varies by ?bloompipe — after OutputPass on the default display pipe, before it under hdr. Ablate + shoot/blackframes before large postFX changes. The look is governed by docs/reference/art-direction.md — per-arena exposure/bloom budgets, no global 'keep it dark' number; screen filters are Storerooms-only.
systems.state-stores: Treat a gameStore field's meaning as a public contract — its 4 subscribers (all keyed off roundPhase; the diagnostics one is ?diag-gated) are the blast radius, and more modules poll getState() on top. Do not deepen the gameState/gameStore dual import (STORE-1).
systems.audio-music-announcer: No loudnorm on loops; respect the per-bus loudness targets. Announcer voice assets are data-driven drop-ins. SD music low-pass is shared-Howler-bus surgery.
systems.ui-hud-menu: index.html is canonical menu markup — never recreate cart-rave-menu.html. hud.js countdown display is presentational; gameplay unlock is gated on phase, not the banner.
systems.input-camera: No lerp/slerp camera smoothing. Keyboard axis easing must match the analog stick deflection simulation.js reads.
systems.scoring-progression: One fall = one KO event fanned to reactors — add a reactor, don't fork the event. A no-score round is a legitimate draw.
systems.shared-protocol: This is the only cross-plane contract — a change here is a change to BOTH client and server. Never duplicate a constant that lives here.
systems.diagnostics-observability: Read-only observers of stores/perf — never mutate game state from here. Keep the __cc* namespace.
systems.dev-tools: Not shipped behavior — safe to iterate, but don't let a harness hook become a runtime dependency of the game.
systems.vfx: Effects are largely host-local today (MP-FX-1) — replicate deliberately, and pool/dispose (shatter size + boost-bar leaks were real bugs).
systems.carts-and-customization: CART_COLORS + the material traverse are the 'Original Rave' invariant (only ART-PALETTE-1 may unfreeze). Pattern UI is blocked on cartrave4 re-UV. New cart surfaces follow the material contract in docs/reference/art-direction.md — no untextured hero material.
systems.game-loop-and-flow: Rounds start only via MSG.gameStart — no tick-level auto-starts in update(). Directive modifiers must not mutate CONFIG mid-round (DIR-1).
systems.ai-bots: Solo rubberband is solo-gated — must not leak into multiplayer. Real bot logic is in simulation.js/gameFlow.js.

rows.item: ROUND-WEDGE-1 — host oscillates `podium ⇄ running` ~25×/s at round end (the wedged-round class, caught live)
rows.notes: **CLOSED 08-03 — Wyatt playtest PASS, and that PASS is what closes `cap-217`.** Phase B (`podiumEndLatch`) held: a full timed round to 0:00 gave one clean podium with no flicker, and the Phase A host-hide check (tab hidden ~30–60 s mid-round) still ended cleanly on podium rather than running forever. Step 5's non-host observation was not run (single machine) and was never the evidence bar. **Do not re-open on the assert alone** — `invariants.js:24` still names `podium→running` while `netcode.js:2835` performs it deliberately, so a first rollback assert remains expected and is not a regression. Original filing below. **Filed 08-01 from cap-217** — the invariant watchdog fired in production, on Wyatt's own machine, and the capture is the evidence. **Elevate to Critical the moment it reproduces**; it is High only because frequency is unknown from n=1. **What the capture holds:** build `2e85f0b` (built 07-31T03:32:59Z), captured **07-31T05:09:05Z**, `is_host=1`, quickplay, `classicRecord`, RTX 4090, tier high, `?diag=1&room=quickplay`. The 512-event ring is **saturated at `EVENT_BUFFER_MAX`** (seq 769..1280) and holds **only two event types**: **171 `assert/phase-transition`, every one `podium → running`**, plus 341 `round/phase` (171 `running→podium` + 170 `podium→running`). It flips on a **~40 ms period** across `t 1283005→1288629` = **5624 ms minimum**; because seq starts at 769, roughly 768 earlier events were already evicted, so that window is the **tail of the storm, not its extent**. Final snapshot: `phase: podium`, `endReason: "timer"`, `winnerSlotIndex: 2`, `remainingMs: null`. **The assert is correct by design, not an over-strict table:** `invariants.js:24` names `podium→running` explicitly as the "wedged round" bug class, and `LEGAL_PHASE_TRANSITIONS.podium = ["countdown", "lobby"]` (`:33`). Two writers are fighting over `gameStore.roundPhase` at round end. **Player-visible**, which is why this outranks the pre-ship polish rows: a results screen re-entering RUNNING 25 times a second is a flickering podium, not a silent log entry. **Not the machine:** cap-215/216 (build `65dea12`, **same 4090, same quickplay, 7 `boot/play-entry` in one session**) carry **zero** asserts — this is not a standing condition of that box. **DO NOT blame ANLX-ATTRACT-1.** `2e85f0b` is the only `src/` commit in `65dea12..2e85f0b` and is therefore the obvious suspect, but it only **subscribes** to `gameStore` and emits analytics — it never writes `roundPhase`, so it cannot produce this. Attributing on adjacency is exactly run-4's "GC metronome" error that **HARNESS-NULL-1** exists to remember. It follows that the regression is either **older than `65dea12` and load/timing-dependent**, or in a path those two clean captures never exercised. **Next evidence, cheapest first:** (a) ✅ **RESOLVED 08-02 — both writers identified by reading the paths, not by adjacency.** Of the three candidates, **quickplay arena rotation is eliminated** and the other two are *both* implicated, fighting each other. **→ RUNNING is [netcode.js:2915](../../src/netcode.js:2915)**, the `MSG.round` applier, which is **not** host-gated; `netcode.js:2835` shows the rollback is *deliberate* — "Server rejected an optimistic host_round … Host may already be on podium while the room is still running — roll back" — with its own `onPodiumRejected` callback. **→ PODIUM is the host's own round-end in [gameFlow.js:149](../../src/gameFlow.js:149)**, gated only on `isHost && phase === "running"`, so the instant a rollback restores `running` the timer-expiry check re-fires `endRound()` on the very next frame, undamped. **The loop:** server MAX-rejects the host's round-end → keeps broadcasting `running` → applier rolls the host back → host immediately re-ends → rejected again, at broadcast rate. That predicts every measured property of cap-217 (host-only, `endReason: "timer"`, ~40 ms period) and explains why cap-215/216 were clean on the same 4090 — the rollback path only opens once the server starts rejecting, so it is not a standing condition of that box. Consistent with the card's own deduction that the cause predates `65dea12`. **Headline consequence: [invariants.js:24](../../src/utils/invariants.js:24) names `podium→running` as *the* wedged-round bug class while `netcode.js:2835` implements it on purpose — the table and the design contradict each other**, so all 171 asserts fired on intended behaviour at that site. Do **not** resolve this by adding `running` to `LEGAL_PHASE_TRANSITIONS.podium`: the oscillation is real and player-visible, and silencing the assert would hide it. The undamped re-entry is **Phase B**, which keeps its own ack. The four unguarded-looking `startRunningAt` sites were checked and cleared: `main.js:4616/4636/4645/4903` are all guarded by `phase === "countdown"`, and `:3041`/`:3126` are `testdrive`-only (cap-217 was quickplay); (b) the ring proves the oscillation but not its origin — the `assert` channel is in `AUTO_CAPTURE_CHANNELS` (`diagnostics.js:51`), so **up to 5 auto-capture bundles existed in memory that session** (`__ccDiag.captures()`, `AUTO_CAPTURE_MAX_PER_SESSION`) holding the pre-storm state and were never uploaded — ✅ **SHIPPED 08-02 `cc09985`**: auto-captures now POST to the same `/api/captures` endpoint F8 uses, so the next occurrence arrives via `npm run captures:pull` instead of dying with the tab. Gating stayed **structural** (auto-capture needs `apiRef` → `installDiagnostics()` → `main.js:5580` under `?diag=1`), pinned by a test so a future unconditional install cannot silently turn players into uploaders; volume bounds are unchanged (5/page-load, 5s debounce, error+assert only); (c) ⏸ **not attempted — deliberately, and not because it was forgotten.** It is listed as "if cheap" and it is not: the loop only opens once the *server* MAX-rejects, so a repro needs the host-hide condition plus a rejecting server, not merely a podium in quickplay. Now that (a) names both writers, a **unit** test against the two call paths is the cheaper next probe. **Instrumentation hazard, same card:** an assert storm **saturates the 512-event ring and evicts every other channel** — cap-217 carries no boot timeline, no perf, no `warmupSettle`, so the single most interesting session produced the least informative capture. ✅ **SHIPPED 08-02 `8063b3e`**: eviction now drops the oldest event from whichever channel occupies the **most** slots, so a flooding channel eats its own evictions and can never push a quiet channel below parity; degrades to FIFO when the storm is the only channel. Chose parity over a per-channel floor constant because the buffer is channel-agnostic and a fixed table would silently stop covering new channels. Dedupe was considered and **not** taken (Wyatt's call — floor is enough). **Does not re-open COUNTDOWN-QUICKPLAY-1** (a different phase edge — countdown entry, not podium exit) or the reverted host-countdown gate (`c8df8fd`).

rows.item: SHOOT-ANIM-1 — `shoot-gpu` captures freeze **all** per-frame level animation
rows.notes: **CLOSED 08-02** — fixed in `6b27283`, `--t` flag in `79a9caf`. **The root cause was one layer up from this card's own diagnosis, and was never capture-specific.** Not LOD, and not `settle()`: [menuAttract.js](../../src/ui/menuAttract.js) runs its own rAF loop that **rendered without ever updating**, while the game loop that owns `levelUpdate` bails in `shouldSkipTiming` whenever `menuVisible` is true — which the harness deliberately keeps true. The attract loop is therefore the *only* loop running during a capture. **The same was true for real players: the live main-menu arena was frozen for everyone** — water static, turbines stopped, beacons dead — so this was a player-facing bug, not only a QA one. **Fixed via the attract loop's new `onAnimationTick` dep, NOT via `settle()` — this card's own option (a), now superseded:** `settle()` only awaits rAF and never renders, so driving animation there lands a frame stale. The tick sits *below* the throttle gate and *before* the render, pairing update→render in one frame exactly as the game loop orders them; `updateLevelLod` keeps local wall time, since a small pinned `t` would park its module-global 250 ms latch in the future. Attract cost now times update+render together, so the auto-quality watchdog can actually see the added CPU. **Verified:** gate-beacon opacity went 0/23 → 11/23 frame-to-frame changes free-running (the attract loop throttles to ~30 fps, so ~every other rAF tick renders); `?t=1000` holds it at exactly `0.6066653819`, matching `0.45 + sin(1000×0.0009)×0.2` analytically; the live menu was confirmed animating on the ordinary no-harness path; zero console errors across 8 captures on real hardware (RTX 4090, not SwiftShader). **Bonus finding — a documented attribution was wrong.** [visual-qa.md](../guides/visual-qa.md) blamed Classic's 15–30% capture-to-capture variance on *crowd animation*, but the crowd was frozen in every capture (that is this very card) and is frozen still. Measured with animation **pinned**, so animation cannot contribute: Classic's null floor is **15.89%**, Sundial's is **~1.2%** (1.22% and 1.21% on two independent pairs). The real cause is **unseeded construction randomness** — `Math.random()` at build time, 56 call sites in `zanzibarPlatform.js` alone, including procedural texture painting, so every page load paints a different arena. Three 08-01 findings had their "evidence" sitting in that variance under the wrong name. Guide corrected; null floors and the two-phase `--t` recipe documented there. Doubles as the null-control arm **HARNESS-NULL-1** asks for, on this one rig. **Deferred → SHOOT-ANIM-2.**

rows.item: SHOOT-ANIM-2 — rave dressing is still frozen in captures
rows.notes: **CLOSED 08-02** (code `33f0d15`). **Playtest seed stripped 08-04** — was reseeding the console under a closed badge. Original verification was agent-side (frame deltas); residual in-round crowd feel is not an open owed card. **CLOSED 08-02** — fixed in `33f0d15`. Body extracted to `tickRaveDressing()` + a shared `raveDressingWanted()` gate, called from the game loop **and** the attract loop; the gates that legitimately differ (frame budget, clock source) stay at the two call sites, so there is one definition and no drift. **Deliberately no frame budget on the attract path:** `frameBudgetAllow` **fails closed** without a preceding `beginFrameBudget` (stale `frameStartMs` → negative remaining), and its `allowCache` is only cleared by `beginFrameBudget`, so the first `false` would **latch that bucket permanently**; calling `beginFrameBudget` from attract instead would put two loops on one set of module globals, and the budget exists to protect host physics, none of which runs at the menu. Weak machines are covered here by the attract cost feed → auto-quality, which steps the tier down and flips `crowdAnimate` off. **Two of the five items this card named were filed on a wrong premise, corrected rather than quietly dropped.** (1) **Lasers and billboard were absent, not frozen** — `finalizeArenaShellForMenu` builds the shell with `includeJuice: false` ([main.js:2615](../../src/main.js:2615)) and the DEV log says "sky + stadium, no lasers" outright, and captures boot through that same menu path, so they were never in a capture to freeze. Left absent by ack; the `raveJuiceInitialized` sub-gate is kept so they animate on their own if the juice is ever built there. (2) **`fxPass.uTime` was never a capture bug — it is a live one**, split out as **FX-TIME-1**. Scope is **Classic Record only** (`levelUsesRaveExtras` is `id === "classicRecord"`). The **record spin** stays game-loop-only on purpose: it is `rotation.y += … * dt`, a delta accumulator coupled to `applySlowMoToDt`, so it cannot pin under `?t=` and would fight slow-mo if converted. **Verified** (dev server, RTX 4090): stage spots + crowd bulbs **0 → 11/23** frame-to-frame changes free-running, and **11/23 on the ordinary no-harness menu path**; **null control at `?preset=low` reports 0/23 on all ten objects while still finding them**, so the probe is provably not blind — a second null-control arm for **HARNESS-NULL-1**. Pinned `--t 500` vs `--t 6783` (6283 ms = exact antiphase for `sin(nowSec×0.5)` **and** 3 half-periods of `sin(nowSec×1.5)`) reads **36.24%** against a **14.51%** same-phase floor, and the amplified diff is decisive where the number alone would not be: searchlight shafts, stage columns and deck rings appear **only** in the signal, while the null carries crowd speckle alone — i.e. unseeded construction randomness, consistent with the ~15.9% Classic floor measured in SHOOT-ANIM-1.

rows.notes:
**ACTIVE — unparked 08-04, Wave 3 acked. Plan for Waves 3–4, with verified line refs and the sweep protocol: [perf-pass-1-handover.md](./perf-pass-1-handover.md) — read it before touching this card.** Wave 3 delivers a **cost menu**, not shipped cuts; no visual cut ships without Wyatt picking it. No visual cut without Wyatt sign-off. Deliberately no long-lived Owed seed on this parent until a cut ships. *(Older "all three arenas" wording below is historical context from the filing.)*
**Filed 08-03 from his Run 8 report**, alongside ATTRACT-JANK-1 below. Report is a felt regression on weak hardware, not a number, so this card is **measure-first and nothing else until there is a delta**: the standing rule from run-4's "GC metronome" error (**HARNESS-NULL-1**) is that adjacency is not attribution. **Known floor to measure against:** run 5 put the Intel UHD iGPU at LOW at **54% of frames over 33 ms** — that is the pre-existing smoothness floor, so "bad on the Intel box" is only evidence if it is *worse than that*. **Method:** bisect recent batches on the Intel box, **prod not dev** — dev-only probes (`__cartRavePerf.scene`, `import("/src/…")`) lie in prod, and dev-server timing is not the shipped bundle. Candidate surface added since the last known-good measurement is large (Sundial god rays + hologram, the three LOAD-POSTER-1 loading scenes, octagon/holo work, FX layers), which is exactly why a bisect beats guessing. **Do not** start tuning tier knobs before a measurement — `PERF-TIER-1` and `PERF-WATCH-1` are the levers *after* attribution, not instead of it. Related: WARM-SOLO-1 (weak-GPU first-draw stalls), PROBE-WARM-RT-1.
**MEASURED 08-03 (Wyatt) — and the card now has a target, which it did not before.** His words: *"all three have less than passable fps on the intel machine. i want the goal to be 60 FPS on low on the intel machine. i took an f8 cap on all three levels."* **That is a spec, not a bug report** — the card stops being "is it worse?" and becomes "hit 60 fps at Low on the Intel UHD box in Cart Rave, Storerooms and Sundial". Note it reframes the known floor rather than clearing it: run 5 measured that box at Low at 54% of frames over 33 ms, i.e. it has **never** held 60, so this is a perf program against an absolute bar, not a regression hunt — do not spend the budget bisecting for a culprit that may not exist. Three F8 captures exist; pull with `npm run captures:pull` and attribute before touching a single knob. **PERF-TIER-1 / PERF-WATCH-1 are levers after attribution.** **ATTRIBUTED 08-03 from his own three captures (cap-236/237/238, build `2c18057`, Intel UHD, `quality_tier: low`, solo, host).** **Read them as one session, not three** — all three are F8 presses inside a single page load, so they share one event ring and the loop counters are **cumulative**; per-capture percentages understate the last arena badly (Cart Rave reads 16.1% cumulative but **27.8%** once diffed). Diffed segments: **Sundial → Storerooms 48.9 fps avg, 10.2% of frames over 33 ms**; **Storerooms → Cart Rave 38.2 fps avg, 27.8% over 33 ms**. **Cart Rave is roughly twice as expensive as the other two** and is where the budget goes first. **Two conclusions that change the plan:** (1) **This is steady-state frame cost, not stalls** — `over66` moves by only 2 and 4 across those segments and `warmupCompile` is a healthy 141 ms / 116 materials, so warm-up, shader compile and hitching are all cleared and the levers are per-frame cost (renderScale, post chain, draw calls / overdraw), **not** warm-up work. (2) **The box is far better than its own documented floor, so there is no regression to hunt** — run 5 put it at **54%** of frames over 33 ms; it is now 10–28%. His report is still correct, but the true statement is "it has never been 60", not "it got worse", so do **not** spend the card bisecting. **Caveat:** each segment carries ~16 s and ~24 s of menu/transition, which is cheaper than gameplay, so in-arena fps is somewhat *worse* than these averages — a per-arena isolation run is the next measurement, not a knob. **And the loop only counts `over33`/`over66`, so nothing currently measures the 16.7 ms bar the target is set at** — closing that instrumentation gap is step one.

rows.item: HARNESS-NULL-1 — no measurement rig has a null-control arm
rows.notes: Process/tooling, not behavior. Every A/B number this repo produces is currently unfalsifiable: no rig can demonstrate it reports ~0 when nothing changed, so warm-up order, run ordering and accumulated state are indistinguishable from a real effect. Seven subjects match nothing, on any of the 11 screens the tool sweeps (menu · customize + its sunglasses and patterns tabs · settings · challenges · how-to · in-match HUD · pause · results podium · touch in-match): **(1) `.cr-touch-btn`** (`cart-rave-menu.css:182`, `:active`) and **(2) `.cr-kbm-toast-close`** (`:178`, `:hover`/`:active`) — both class names appear in **zero `.js`/`.ts`/`.html` files repo-wide**; the CSS is all that is left of them. **(3) `.cr-level-btn`** (`:529` `:hover:not(.cr-level-btn--disabled)`, `:2400` inside the designed focus ring, `:3289` in the reduced-motion block) — the arena radiogroup at `index.html:703` carries the `hidden` attribute and its own comment calls it a "hidden radiogroup: arena data source"; the visible control is the `.cr-arena-page` pager. That also means the nine-selector designed focus ring at `:2398-2409` is an **eight**-selector ring in practice. **(4-6) `a`, `select`, `[role="button"]`** — three of the five element types listed in the unscoped fallback ring at `src/ui/loadingScreen.css:577`; no `<select>` and no `role="button"` element exists anywhere, and the only `<a>` elements created are transient download links (`main.js:5604`, `postFxDebug.js:190/241`). Harmless defensive CSS, but it means that rule is doing two-fifths of the work it looks like it does. All seven are held in `DECLARED_UNREACHABLE` in `tools/states.mjs` with these reasons, printed on stdout every run and in the montage banner — **and if any of them ever starts matching again the run says so out loud**, so declaring them does not hide a future regression.

rows.item: TOUCH-HOVER-1 — no `@media (hover: hover)` guard anywhere, so hover states latch on touch
rows.notes: **Measured 07-31 by `npm run states`** (FIGHT-VERIFY-1 Phase B) on a `hasTouch + isMobile` 390×844 client. There are **zero** occurrences of the `(hover:` media feature in `src/**/*.css` — the only three hover-capability checks in the repo live in JS (`touchControls.js:580`, `rotatePrompt.js:124`, `device.js:36`) — so every `:hover` rule applies on a coarse-pointer device, where a tap latches it until the user taps elsewhere. Reported as **one aggregate advisory row**, not one failure per selector: it is one missing media query, and 30-odd reds would drown the tally. Measured with `CSS.forcePseudoState`, **not** synthetic mouse input — Chromium under mobile emulation routes `mouse.move()` through the touch pipeline and produces no `:hover` at all, which made an earlier mouse-driven pass under-report this (1/6) before the method was corrected. Result on two consecutive runs: **2 of the 5** (run B: 2 of 4) hover rules whose subject is actually on screen at 390×844 still repaint — `.cr-reroll` and `.cr-plate .cr-plate-btn`. The denominator is small because the phone menu shows fewer controls, and the non-repainting remainder are exactly the dead ones filed as **MENU-CMD-FEEL-1** / **MENU-NAME-HOVER-1** — i.e. **every hover rule that has a live delta at all does apply on touch**. Low because the visual result is mild (a re-roll button and a plate button staying lit after a tap), but it belongs to the same pass as UI-SCALE-1's ≤768 reflow.

Two passes per [responsive-scale-migration.md](./responsive-scale-migration.md): fluid root + rem clamps; media queries stay px. **Pass 1 also does ≤768 reflow — phone = fewer elements.** SHEET-1 unblocked (tool exists). Sequential single-owner. Safety: ≥1920 pixel-identical pre/post.

fragile_systems.why: The `callbacks` seam is THREE sites, not two: the default stub in netcode.js's callbacks literal → the registerGameCallbacks adapter → the impl in buildNetcodeGameBridge. The adapter RENAMES (bridge `onHopLand` → literal `onHopLandRef`), so literal and bridge keys do not match — only adapter↔bridge are name-coupled. Miss a site and you get a silent no-op, not an error. MSG.* is NOT hand-mirrored: shared/protocol.js is one module imported by both planes — never duplicate a key that lives there.

Host-authoritative + migration invariants: promote-oldest ON DISCONNECT (lobby quality rebalance can override it via pickPreferredHostId once the score margin is cleared), #lastSeq reset, P2P teardown/re-init. A rewrite reopens closed NET-* bugs (explicitly NOT pre-ship work). getConnections() is an iterator.

Rapier is host-AUTHORITATIVE — the host is sole authority for NPCs and remote inputs, but every predicting client steps the same world locally (gameLoop.js client-prediction branch); do not assume the host is the sole peer running physics. castRay exclude wants the object not the .handle (silent exclusion disable); collision logic must not move server-side.
main.js is a single closure — a moved inner function silently drops out of the callbacks/deps bundle. Carving it is MAIN-1 (deferred); until then expect the closure.
The composer pass ORDER is load-bearing (toneMapping no-ops without OutputPass; envMapIntensity no-ops against scene.environment). Ablate + shoot/blackframes before postFX rewrites.

A gameStore field's meaning is depended on by 4 subscribers with no syntactic link, all keyed off roundPhase — changing it silently changes announcer/directive/analytics behavior. The diagnostics subscriber is ?diag-gated, so fewer are live in an ordinary session; many more modules poll getState(), which widens the blast radius of a rename.
